audit_findings.title: Post-deal shares and balance sheet are paired with pre-Worldpay earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 42.780 million acquisition shares, equal to 14.7% of the 291.424 million-share denominator; Worldpay contributed $2.6 billion of H1 2026 revenue, but its owner earnings are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation divides pre-Worldpay owner earnings by a post-close share count and combines them with a post-close balance-sheet bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The financial results of Worldpay will be consolidated by the Company beginning as of the acquisition date.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a forecast risk. Including the acquisition shares without the corresponding Worldpay owner earnings dilutes per-share value, while the post-close cash, debt and disposed-business effects can move value in other directions. The 14.7% share mismatch is large enough to affect the valuation conclusion, but the net direction cannot be established without post-close owner earnings.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild the valuation on one post-close date using Worldpay earnings, removal of Issuer Solutions, post-close financing costs, integration spending, unrestricted cash and the fully reconciled diluted share count.

audit_findings.title: The anchor lacks a full-period cost for the debt whose principal is not deducted
audit_findings.magnitude: The $6.2 billion November 2025 notes carry $310.75 million of annual cash coupon interest, equal to 18.5% of the $1.680 billion anchor; H1 2026 interest expense increased $204.1 million year over year
audit_findings.mechanism: Because debt principal is not deducted from the equity bridge, its recurring interest, issuance-cost amortization and hedge effects must be fully reflected in owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: In April 2025, we obtained bridge financing that was terminated in November 2025 when we issued $6.2 billion in senior unsecured notes as described in "Note 9—Long-Term Debt and Lines of Credit" in the accompanying consolidated financial statements.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated: FY2025 includes only a short interest stub on the transaction notes, whereas the valuation capitalizes that year's owner earnings as though it contained the recurring financing burden. The $310.75 million annual coupon alone is material relative to the anchor and could change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Calculate a full-year interest schedule for all June 30, 2026 debt, including variable-rate debt, discounts, issuance costs and hedge effects, align it with the post-close earnings perimeter and rerun owner earnings without separately deducting ordinary debt principal.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may add settlement and customer money that is not available to common holders
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.711 billion excess bridge addition: $5.409 billion added versus $1.698 billion filed as available for general purposes; $12.73 per supplied diluted share and 12.4% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Unavailable settlement, reserve and customer cash is added directly to the common-equity bridge without the associated claims.
audit_findings.evidence: The available cash of $980.7 million does not include the following: (i) settlement-related cash balances, (ii) funds held as collateral for merchant losses ("Merchant Reserves") (iii) certain funds held for customers and (iv) proceeds from our November Senior Notes offering which were reserved to fund our planned acquisition of Worldpay.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates that only $1.698 billion of the $5.409 billion cash balance was available for general purposes. Adding the full balance therefore overstates the bridge by $3.711 billion unless separate evidence establishes additional distributable cash. Mechanically removing that excess would reduce base value from $102.47 to about $89.74 per share, below the $92.54 market price, so it can reverse the base conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile June 30, 2026 cash account by account to settlement obligations, customer funds, merchant reserves, regulatory restrictions and escrow, then rerun the bridge using only distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: A disposal gain may have been capitalized as recurring owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $331.4 million pretax Payroll Solutions gain, equal to 19.7% of the $1.680 billion anchor; the related after-tax owner-earnings effect is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any retained after-tax disposal gain inflates the owner-earnings anchor and is projected through the explicit forecast and terminal value; the 2024 gain can also distort historical growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Consolidated operating income and operating margin for the year ended December 31, 2025 included the effects of a $331.4 million gain on the sale of Payroll Solutions compared to a gain of $273.1 million for the sale of AdvancedMD in the prior year.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved accounting-treatment possibility, not a demonstrated inclusion error. However, the filed gain is large enough relative to the anchor that retaining it would be reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion. The $273.1 million AdvancedMD gain creates the same unresolved issue in the growth history.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $331.4 million and $273.1 million gains, their tax effects, contingent-consideration remeasurements and related cash-flow adjustments through the OE workpaper, confirming that each nonrecurring effect was removed exactly once.

audit_findings.title: The anchor embeds a large, non-steady mixture of acquisition and transformation costs
audit_findings.magnitude: $737.5 million of 2025 acquisition and transformation expense, equal to 43.9% of the $1.680 billion anchor and $429.0 million above 2024; H1 2026 acquisition, transformation and transaction expense was $585.1 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining temporary costs depresses the OE anchor and projected growth, while removing recurring or still-required costs inflates OE; the treatment also affects the forecast through the integration period.
audit_findings.evidence: Operating income included acquisition and transformation expenses of $737.5 million and $308.5 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, which were primarily included within Corporate selling, general and administrative expenses.
audit_findings.explanation: The expenses are filed, but the valuation's treatment of them is unresolved. Their scale is clearly material. Treating all costs as permanent would likely understate value, while eliminating all of them would overstate value because transformation and integration activities are expected to continue through 2028.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the expenses by cash versus noncash, transaction-close versus integration or transformation, recurring versus temporary and expected completion year; retain recurring costs and explicitly forecast temporary costs before rerunning OE.

audit_findings.title: A probable redeemable-NCI obligation is absent from the common-equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Total filed redeemable noncontrolling interests were $210.757 million at June 30, 2026, an upper-bound bridge effect of $0.72 per supplied diluted share and 0.7% of the $29.863 billion base equity value; the Greece-specific amount is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An undeducted redemption payment overstates the common-equity bridge, partly offset by the additional subsidiary earnings obtained upon redemption.
audit_findings.evidence: The option held by the minority shareholder in Greece, which is redeemable at a price other than fair value, is considered probable of becoming redeemable on June 30, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated, although the Greece-specific settlement amount and acquired earnings are not disclosed. Even deducting the entire filed redeemable-NCI balance—an upper bound because it includes other subsidiaries—would reduce base value by only about $0.72 per share. That is too small to change the valuation conclusion relative to the $9.93 gap between base value and market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the Greece option was exercised, isolate its settlement price and funding, and verify that any incremental subsidiary earnings are treated consistently; update the bridge even though the current filed upper bound is not material.
